title: Analog Days: No Internet Access
description: 9:00 AM – 7:00 PM · On Monday and Tuesday, August 3rd and 4th , the Marmot library system will undergo a planned server upgrade. During this time, some of our library services will be temporarily unavailable while important system maintenance is completed. The following services will be unavailable: Internet access at the library Sierra (staff circulation system) The online library catalog Public printing Libby (unless you are already logged in) Online databases New York Times access Libby Users If you use Libby for ebooks or audiobooks, please log in before Monday, August 3rd . If you are already signed in, you'll be able to continue reading and listening during the outage. However, you will not be able to log in, create a new account, or borrow new titles while the system is offline. We also recommend downloading any books you'd like to enjoy during the outage in advance. …

title: Eco-Series- Between Grief and Gratitude
description: 8:30 AM – 10:00 AM · Between Grief & Gratitude Where Love and Loss Meet in a Changing World Join Lauren Norton of Through the Woods Doula, Mollie Theis of EcoAction Partners and the Wilkinson Public Library for a four-part series on navigating climate anxiety and eco-grief. The first two sessions will consist of a facilitated community conversation connecting our love of these landscapes with the challenge of the climate crisis at our doorsteps. After exploring our shared relationship with the current reality, the second two sessions will provide opportunities to express pain, grief, love and hope through various mediums including local poetry and group art projects.

title: The Legacy of Julia Child's Kitchen with Smithsonian Curator Paula J. Johnson
description: 12:00 PM – 1:00 PM · Join us for a conversation that's sure to warm your heart (and make your stomach rumble), as we delve into the legacy of cooking icon Julia Child with Smithsonian curator and public historian Paula J. Johnson, author of Julia Child's Kitchen : The Design, Tools, Stories, and Legacy of an Iconic Space . The book includes interviews with chefs who knew Julia well, commentary on her favorite culinary tools and kitchen gadgets, and a stunning array of photos. Julia Child's 20' x 14' kitchen was a serious workspace and recipe‑testing lab that exuded a sense of mid‑century homey comfort. It has been on display at the National Museum of American History in Washington, D.C., for most of the past twenty-three years, and museum goers have made it a top destination. …
